findings.claim: Immediate selection evidence is weak and only marginally coherent: the compressed-choice excess fixed-frame RMS is small (whole-window mean ~0.081 A, CI95 ~0.070-0.092) and top-4 teacher overlap is near chance (~0.47), while chosen-teacher score correlations are low (~0.06-0.10). Selection therefore carries little reliable signal about which candidates are better, so direction priorities should not be set from point estimates of selection quality alone.

Descendant survival credit is available but not equivalent to final affinity benefit: survival enrichment is computed over 14 independent batches with BH correction jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests, and the lineage table records terminal metadata at score time 0.99/state time 1.0 with one future-resampling node per batch. No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied, so last-record survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Ancestral coverage is thin and survivor-biased: of 700 total batch nodes, 349 have fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 have fewer than 6, with at most 2 teachers per batch. Survival-conditioned credit is therefore dominated by shallow-lineage nodes, and any survival-quality comparison is confounded by this coverage imbalance.

Among the survival-enrichment rows read, only landmark_00_soft_mass shows a nominally positive effect (z~0.365, positive batch fraction 0.857) but its q~0.12 does not survive multiplicity adjustment; local derivative and curvature features (dx, dy, dz, cxx, cyy) are null or negative with q>=0.30. This is a concrete case where multiplicity-adjusted support changes the ranking relative to raw p-values.

The curve-support selection rule is explicit (absolute integrated z>=0.1, batch direction fraction>=0.857, q<0.05, scale floor excluded) and selects 24 curves, but the curve-fidelity audit is delivered only as a container summary (24 items, keys preview only). Fit fidelity and sign-change details for those curves are not yet read, so no validated time-conditioned contrast rule can be asserted from this evidence.

hypotheses.falsifier: survival_enrichment_z for landmark_00_soft_mass fails to exceed the incumbent's value with q<0.05 under the same 14-batch BH procedure
hypotheses.observable: survival_enrichment_z for landmark_00_soft_mass over the observed window
hypotheses.scope: coordinate reward only; no affinity-head derivative; no temperature change
hypotheses.statement: A landmark_00 soft-mass coordinate reward (soft occupancy/mass at landmark 0) would increase descendant survival enrichment relative to the incumbent static reward, because soft_mass is the only survival feature with a positive point estimate and high batch-direction consistency.

hypotheses.falsifier: selected curves exceed relative RMSE 0.35 or contain strong sign conflicts, in which case the constant rule is retained
hypotheses.observable: relative_node_RMSE and sign_changes for the selected contrast curves
hypotheses.scope: registered temporal_region recipe only; static teachers unchanged
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule derived from validated observed-node contrast curves would outperform a constant rule, but only if the selected 24 curves show acceptable fit fidelity (relative RMSE<=0.35) and no strong sign conflicts.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record survival credit cannot be interpreted as final affinity benefit, and the immediate-selection versus descendant-quality comparison remains unavailable.
The curve-fidelity audit is delivered only as a container summary; per-curve fit fidelity, sign changes and rate changes were not read, so no validated time-conditioned contrast rule is asserted.
Survival and increment effects are observational and multiplicity-adjusted; they are not causal selection effects or atom-velocity forces.
Ancestral coverage is shallow (349 nodes <3 ancestors, 531 <6), so survival-conditioned comparisons are confounded by survivor bias and parent weighting.
No current-study outcome data are available to this role; all statements are descriptive of supplied diagnostics.
